body: The diagram below shows how olive oil is produced. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features.

chart.title: The production of extra virgin olive oil
steps: Olives are harvested by hand or by machines that shake the trees
Harvested olives are transported to the mill in ventilated crates
Leaves and twigs are removed by a blower
Olives are washed in cold water
Olives, including stones, are crushed into a paste
The paste is slowly mixed (malaxation) for 30–40 minutes
A centrifuge separates the oil from water and solids
Solid waste is used as fuel or fertiliser
Oil is left to settle in stainless steel tanks
Oil is filtered and bottled in dark glass

body: The diagram below shows how sea water is turned into drinking water at a desalination plant. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features.

chart.title: Producing drinking water by reverse osmosis desalination
steps: Sea water is drawn in through an offshore intake pipe
Screens remove fish, seaweed and large debris
Water passes through sand filters to remove fine particles
Chemicals are added to prevent scaling
High-pressure pumps force water through reverse osmosis membranes
Concentrated brine is diluted and returned to the sea
Minerals such as calcium are added back to the fresh water
Water is disinfected with chlorine
Treated water is stored in a reservoir
Water is pumped to homes through the mains supply

body: The diagram below illustrates the stages in the production of silk cloth. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features.

chart.title: The life cycle of the silkworm and the production of silk cloth
steps: Silk moth lays around 500 eggs
Eggs hatch into larvae after 10 days
Silkworms feed on mulberry leaves for 4–6 weeks
Silkworm spins a cocoon over 3–8 days
Some cocoons are allowed to develop into moths, restarting the cycle
Remaining cocoons are boiled to soften them
Silk threads are unwound from the cocoons
Threads are twisted together and dyed
Dyed thread is woven into silk cloth

body: The diagram below shows how waste paper is recycled. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features.

chart.title: Recycling waste paper
steps: Used paper is collected from households and offices
Paper is sorted by type and grade at a recycling centre
Bales of paper are taken to a paper mill
Paper is mixed with water and chemicals to form pulp
Pulp is screened to remove staples, plastic and glue
Ink is removed by adding soap and blowing air through the pulp
Pulp is bleached if white paper is required
Pulp is sprayed onto a moving mesh to form a sheet
Rollers press out water and heated cylinders dry the sheet
Paper is wound onto large reels and cut to size

body: The diagram below shows how electricity is generated at a geothermal power station. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features.

chart.title: Generating electricity from geothermal energy
steps: A production well is drilled 4–5 km into hot rock
Cold water is pumped down an injection well
Water is heated by the hot rocks underground
Hot water rises up the production well under pressure
In the flash tank, pressure falls and water turns to steam
Steam drives a turbine
The turbine powers a generator which produces electricity
Electricity is sent to the grid through transmission lines
Steam is cooled in a condenser and becomes water again
Water is returned to the injection well

body: The diagram below shows the process of making chocolate from cocoa beans. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features.

chart.title: How chocolate is made
steps: Ripe cocoa pods are harvested from cacao trees
Pods are split open and beans are removed
Beans are fermented under banana leaves for 5–7 days
Beans are dried in the sun
Beans are shipped to a chocolate factory
Beans are roasted at 120–140°C
Shells are removed, leaving cocoa nibs
Nibs are ground into a thick cocoa liquor
Sugar, milk and cocoa butter are mixed in
Mixture is heated and cooled repeatedly (tempering)
Chocolate is poured into moulds and set

body: The diagram below shows how a farm uses animal waste to produce energy and fertiliser. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features.

chart.title: Producing biogas from animal waste on a farm
steps: Manure from cattle sheds is collected in a slurry pit
Slurry is mixed with crop waste in a mixing tank
Mixture is pumped into a sealed digester
Bacteria break down the material without oxygen for 20–30 days
Methane-rich biogas collects under the digester dome
Gas is cleaned to remove moisture and hydrogen sulphide
Biogas fuels an engine that generates electricity and heat
Heat warms the farmhouse and digester
Leftover digestate is stored in a lagoon
Digestate is spread on fields as fertiliser
